The nbfx Shell is the generic JavaFX application shell: docked and detached window groups, tab panes, sliding side areas, the toolbar container and the file drag-and-drop bridge. Applications assemble their workbench from these pieces.
The shell knows nothing about projects, Java sources or IDE actions. The window model lives in nbfx.platform.workspace; the shell renders it and resolves host services from the global Lookup. IDE-specific contributions (tab titles, tab context menus, project status) stay in nbfx.ide.workbench.
The IDE workbench builds its editor area from NbfxTabPane and Docking.
A downstream product reuses the same shell with its own views and actions.
Files dropped from the desktop open in the application.
The API is under development until the MVP freeze; the shell is exercised by the IDE and platform smoke tests.
A JDK is required only to compile; JavaFX is provided by the runtime.
Only org.netbeans.modules.nbfx.platform.shell is public.
The shell resolves WindowEnvironment, EditorContext and the content services from the global Lookup.
The host module registers its implementations, not this module.
None.
The platform stylesheet is bundled as styles.css.
None.
The shell runs on the JavaFX Application Thread, like the window system itself.
No code runs on startup.
No code runs on exit.
No special requirements.
